This has the un-/intended effect of what we describe as ‘emotional shrinkage’, the suppression of time, space, and inclination, for imagining and realising love for self and others. In this context, gestures of love can be understood as acts of conscious resistance. Exploring our own experiences of this exposes the emotional labour and career deceleration of an unwillingness to neglect and exploit, but more importantly reveals its deeply emancipatory impact. papers.summary: Drawing on a one-year ethnography in Shenzhen’s tech zone (2023-2024) composed of individual interviews, textual analysis, and participant observations, this thesis develops an interpretive phenomenological analysis of working time and temporalities situated in the post-socialist context of contemporary urban China. Theoretically, this thesis synthesises critical scholarship at the intersection of time and temporality, technology, and labour, highlighting the productive tensions between the social arrangement of time and embodied experiences of time. Accordingly, the thesis is organised around their juxtaposition. Seeing time as a medium of socio-political power, the thesis first explores the normative temporal order in post-socialist China through urban and digital media artefacts.
